title: Lesson 73: Cost Architecture for Enterprise AI: Token Budgets, Infrastructure, and FinOps
description: How to architect the cost of an enterprise agent system: the three-lever cost identity, cost per completed task as the operating metric, token budgets and throughput planning, the self-hosted versus managed-API crossover, and FinOps attribution.

questions.question: Why is cost per completed task a better metric to manage than cost per token?
options: Per-token prices fall while total bills rise, because work per task grows faster and hidden retries stay invisible
Per-token pricing is never published by providers at all, so the figure cannot be reconciled against a monthly invoice or used in a forecast
Per-token cost counts only generated output and ignores every input token the agent sends
Per-token cost is always the higher figure, so finance has more room to negotiate a lower contract
questions.explanation: A task bill grows even as unit prices fall, because the work one task performs multiplies across planning, tool calls, retries, and sub-agents. Cost per completed task captures that real spend, while cost per token hides it.

questions.question: A change cuts the context sent on each call but causes noticeably more model calls. Under the three-lever cost identity, what is the likely result?
options: It always saves money because context size is the only lever that reduces total cost directly, with no downside at all
It always loses money because any extra call doubles the effective per-token price of the task
The saving on context size can be spent back on call count, because the two multiply toward break-even
It has no cost effect because output cost is independent of both context size and call count
questions.explanation: Total cost is a product of three levers: context size, call count, and effective per-token price. A gain on one lever that spends on another can cancel out, so optimizations must be judged against all three at once.

questions.question: A team weighs moving a high-volume workload from a managed model API to self-hosted GPUs. What rule should decide it?
options: Self-host whenever the task is narrow, regardless of how heavily the purchased hardware is actually used
Stay on the managed API always, because per-token prices fall faster than hardware costs
Choose based on enthusiasm for open-weight models rather than on measured consumption
Move it only once sustained utilization clears the crossover, since idle GPUs are billed anyway
questions.explanation: Managed APIs price per token with no idle cost, while self-hosting shifts to fixed hourly cost that is wasteful when idle and efficient only at high utilization. The decision follows the crossover against measured utilization.
